Greek Ports and Payment Systems Disrupted Amid Ongoing Cyber Attack

A coordinated cyber attack targeting Greece’s port and payment infrastructure is causing widespread disruption to economic activity across the country, industry sources confirmed Thursday.

The attack, which began early Wednesday, has affected digital systems at several of Greece’s largest commercial ports, including Piraeus and Thessaloniki, as well as major payment clearing networks. The Ministry of Digital Governance stated that while port operations have not ground to a halt, delays in customs processing and cargo clearance are accumulating, with some container movements slowed by over 36 hours.

“Authorities are working around the clock to contain this sophisticated cyber incident,” said Deputy Minister of Digital Governance, Eleni Papadaki. “Our immediate priority is to restore critical services and safeguard ongoing transactions.”

Reports from port operators indicate that gate access control, vessel scheduling, and cargo tracking systems are currently operating in manual or degraded modes. The Hellenic Association of Freight Forwarders warned that if the attack is not contained within the next 48 hours, there could be a backlog of up to 5,000 containers across Greek ports. “Exporters and importers are already facing significant uncertainty. The knock-on effect on supply chains will intensify if the disruption continues,” said association president Giorgos Manolis.

Local payment processors, including the Athens-based PaySmart Solutions, are reporting intermittent outages affecting both retail and business-to-business transactions. Some point-of-sale systems in Athens and Thessaloniki supermarkets have reverted to cash-only sales, according to the Panhellenic Retail Union. Tourists and residents have reported difficulties accessing banking apps and completing electronic payments, particularly in the islands.

The Bank of Greece has confirmed that the core banking system remains secure, but urged vigilance and advised financial institutions to activate contingency plans.

Cybersecurity analysts suggest the attack bears hallmarks of a coordinated ransomware campaign, but investigations are ongoing. “This is a stark reminder of the vulnerabilities in interconnected infrastructure,” said Dr. Ioanna Kouris, a cybersecurity expert at the Hellenic Technology Institute. “The economic impact will escalate unless digital resilience measures are rapidly deployed.”
